name: tool definition
wording: What an agent sees of a capability, as it sees the harness's own tools: names and verbs that are the names of the concepts the capability serves, in their context's words, each with its purpose and when to reach for it, so the definition alone says what it does. The capability states it once, its command help drawn from the same statement; each harness only renders it into its own form, and no skill or prose restates it, so agents call the tool rather than follow instructions about it.
reason: The operator: the design state a session reads was long human prose restating facts across concepts and carrying decisions with their situations; its reader is a model, so the state is the design alone, each concept as its established name and residue, and decisions and their reasons are history. Restated as its established name and residue, standalone, each fact in the one concept it belongs to, with the meaning standing decisions carried folded in. Named tool definition, the established term, in place of capability interface.
